Thanks for the call earlier today, Irene. Quick recap from our side:

- Primary goal: reduce clinician summarization time for discharge notes by ~40% while preserving key findings and safety-critical items.
- Dataset: 50k de-identified encounter notes available for benchmarking; we can provide a 5k holdout set.
- Latency target: p95 < 400ms for average 512-token outputs in production.
- Budget: prototype cap at $Xk/month; if fit looks good, we can scale.

Appreciate the suggested model shortlist you mentioned. Two asks before we commit to the pilot:
1) Can you share the benchmark scripts/metric definitions you use for quality (Rouge, clinical entity recall, hallucination checks)?
2) We want a clear read on quantization impact (quality vs throughput) — particularly if you run AWQ vs GPTQ vs an FP8 path.

Happy to move forward with a small pilot if we can see a quantitative trade table and an actionable pilot plan.

Cheers,
Elena

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Cc: Dr. Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@novasys.io>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-26T09:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call summary & quantization pilot ask — MedSummarizer fit

Elena — thanks again for the time. Attached are the benchmark CSV and the prompt set we discussed (promptset_med_summ_v2.jsonl) plus a short "quant tradeoffs" one-pager. High level answers below and proposed next steps.

Quick answers:
- Benchmarks: we run Rouge-L, F1 on clinical entity extraction (custom NER), average token-level hallucination score (internal regressor), and a clinician-rated fidelity sample (n=200). Scripts and metric definitions: link in the Drive (listed below).
- Recommended models for initial pilot (tiered):
  - Option A (best quality): longform-13B-chat (fp16 baseline) — highest fidelity, p95 latency ~650ms on a single A100 equivalent; best for recall-sensitive cases.
  - Option B (balanced): medical-summarizer-7B (AWQ-4bit build) — we see ~1.8x throughput vs fp16 with <1.5% drop in entity recall in our med datasets.
  - Option C (low-latency): distilled-clinical-3B (GPTQ 4-bit) — p95 ~260–320ms, lower recall on rare entities; good for triage UI.
- Quantization trade summary (short):
  - AWQ (4-bit): keeps layer normalization behavior intact, generally lower quality delta vs fp16 for generation-heavy summarization; best throughput/quality balance in our tests.
  - GPTQ (4-bit per-tensor/per-channel): slightly faster in some kernels but can introduce brittle token-level regressions on long context; may require per-layer tuning.
  - FP8 (hardware-dependent): near-fp16 parity on many quality metrics but requires specialized kernels and brings stability risk on mixed-precision pipelines. Not yet recommended for prototyping unless you have constrained infra and want minimal quality loss.

Proposed pilot (4 weeks):
1) Redwood runs 3-model pilot on your 5k holdout: longform-13B-chat (fp16 baseline), medical-summarizer-7B (AWQ-4), distilled-clinical-3B (GPTQ-4).
2) We'll produce per-example metrics (Rouge-L, NER-F1, hallucination-score) + latency/throughput at target batch sizes and p95 latency.
3) Deliverable: trade table, annotated failure cases (n=200), and recommended production config (batching, KV cache, quant profile).

Next steps: if that works, can you: (a) share the 5k holdout (or give Drive access), and (b) confirm we can spin test VMs in your dev env or provide sample logs for realistic latency simulation?

Attaching: novasy-bench CSV (sanitized), promptset_med_summ_v2.jsonl, quant-tradeoffs-one-pager.pdf

Thanks — looping Rishi & Priyom to scope the quant experiments.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-27T11:08:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call summary & quantization pilot ask — technical notes

Forwarding Novasys thread — a few internal notes for scope and risks before we run the pilot:

- Data / privacy: confirm the holdout has been de-identified and we have a signed DPA for ephemeral test artifacts. If Novasys wants Redwood to run in their VPC, we'll need our Private onboarding checklist.
- Evaluation sampling: use stratified sampling by note length and specialty (ED, cardiology, med-surg) for the 200 clinician-rated cases.
- AWQ vs GPTQ: propose we run a small ablation where we quantize only the last 4 transformer blocks with GPTQ to see if regressions concentrate there. That lets us measure marginal loss vs full-model AWQ.
- FP8: we should avoid for initial pilot — requires extra kernel testing and can introduce non-determinism for some seeds. Flagging to Product/Infra if Novasys insists.

Action items for us:
1) Priyom: prep a script to run per-example metrics and produce a trade table CSV; include time-to-first-token and p95.
2) Rishi: prepare AWQ & GPTQ build configurations for medical-summarizer-7B and distilled-clinical-3B.
3) Irene: request Drive access + DPA from Novasys and confirm whether they prefer Redwood-hosted tests or VPC-run.

Rishi
